slide.title: One Video, Seven Pieces
slide.body: A central video tile with arrows to seven smaller tiles: 3 short videos · carousel · professional post · newsletter · blog. Small tag: AI for Content Creators · Lesson 11.

scenes.on_screen_text: One day of work, one week of content
scenes.voiceover: You spent a whole day making one excellent tutorial video. It gets posted once, and a week later, nobody sees it. What if that one day of work could fill a week of content, on four different channels?

slide.title: What is repurposing?
slide.body: One large 'core piece' circle (blog post, video, webinar) with arrows to several smaller circles labelled by channel.

scenes.voiceover: Welcome to week three, where you build your campaign. We start with repurposing. Repurposing means turning one core piece of content into several new pieces for different channels. The core piece is usually the one that took the most work, such as a blog post, a video or a webinar.

slide.title: Channels are different
slide.body: Short-video platforms: vertical, fast, one idea, captions · Image-led feeds: strong visual, carousel, short caption · Professional networks: a clear insight for decision-makers

scenes.voiceover: But repurposing is not copying. Each channel has a different audience, format and length. Short-video platforms are vertical, fast and visual, with one idea per video. Image-led feeds want a strong visual or a carousel. Professional networks want a clear insight for colleagues and decision-makers.

slide.title: Channels are different
slide.body: Email newsletters: depth, personal tone, a useful link · Blogs and websites: long, searchable, headings. Footer in red: Same text everywhere = poor results.

scenes.voiceover: Newsletter readers chose to hear from you, so they expect more depth and a personal tone. And blogs are long and searchable, with headings people can return to. When you paste the same text everywhere, it usually performs poorly. A caption written for a short video makes no sense in an email.

slide.title: A repurposing prompt
slide.body: Turn this tutorial transcript into a 5-slide carousel for a design-learning audience. One tip per slide, maximum 20 words per slide.

scenes.voiceover: AI is very useful here. Give it the core content, such as a transcript, and ask for one specific new format. For example, turn this tutorial into a five-slide carousel, with one tip per slide and no more than twenty words each. Then edit each piece, and check that nothing new and untrue was added.
For every new piece, ask one question. What changes for this audience? Write the answer in one sentence. If the answer is nothing, you are copying, not repurposing.

scenes.stock_query: large pot of cooked rice kitchen
scenes.voiceover: Repurposing is like cooking one large pot of rice. From the same pot, you can make fried rice, a rice salad and rice pudding. The base is the same, but each dish is prepared differently, for a different meal and different people.

scenes.stock_query: person editing photo on smartphone cafe
scenes.voiceover: Let's see an example. Lucas is a content creator in Lisbon, Portugal. He teaches beginners how to edit photos on a phone. He recorded one twelve-minute tutorial called five edits that fix most phone photos. With AI's help, he turns it into seven pieces of content.

slide.title: Pieces 1 to 4
slide.body: 3 short vertical videos: one edit each, hook in 2 seconds → people scrolling quickly · 5-slide carousel with before/after → people who want a quick reference

scenes.voiceover: First, he asks the AI for a summary of his transcript with timestamps. Then he asks for each format separately. Three short vertical videos, one edit in each, with a hook in the first two seconds for people scrolling quickly. And a carousel of five slides with before and after images, for people who want a quick reference.

slide.title: Pieces 5 to 7
slide.body: Professional post: fix product photos before paying for ads → business owners · Newsletter section: his worst photo story + link → loyal subscribers · Blog post with headings → people searching for answers

scenes.voiceover: He writes a professional post about why small businesses should fix their product photos before paying for ads. That is a business angle, for owners. A newsletter section tells a personal story about his worst photo, for subscribers who already trust him. And a blog post with headings is searchable, for people looking for answers.

slide.title: Check every repurposed piece
slide.body: Red, struck through: "Better photos double sales." Green replacement: a real client story, customers asked fewer questions after the photos improved.

scenes.voiceover: But the AI draft of the professional post claims that better photos double sales. Lucas has no evidence for this. So he replaces it with his own experience, a client whose customers asked fewer questions after the photos improved.

The most common mistake is to change only the length. A shorter version of the same text is still written for the wrong audience. And when AI adapts content, it may add numbers or promises that were not in the original. Review every repurposed piece as if it were new.

slide.title: Key takeaways
slide.body: 1. One core piece → many channel pieces. 2. Channels differ: audience, format, length. 3. Write what changes; check for added claims.

scenes.voiceover: Let's recap. First, repurposing turns one core piece of content into several new pieces for different channels. Second, channels differ in audience, format and length, so copying the same text everywhere usually performs poorly. Third, for each new piece, write what changes for that audience, and check that the AI did not add untrue details.

Now it is your turn. In the exercise below, choose one piece of your content, and use AI to repurpose it into at least four formats. Under each one, write one sentence about what you changed for that audience. It takes about thirty minutes. These pieces can feed your capstone campaign. In the next lesson, Planning a Thirty-Day Campaign Calendar, we start the capstone itself. See you there.
